Devious describes a person or behavior that is clever, indirect, and dishonest — someone who uses hidden, sneaky methods to get what they want, instead of being open and straightforward.

A devious person does not come to you directly or honestly. They quietly scheme, manipulate, and trick their way toward a goal, all while hiding their true motives. On the surface, they might seem perfectly normal — even friendly. But underneath, they are calculating and plotting in ways that others cannot easily see.

Think of it like this: if you want to reach a destination, an honest person walks down the main road openly. A devious person sneaks through hidden back alleys, takes secret shortcuts, and uses every trick possible — not because the main road is blocked, but because they prefer the sneaky approach.
What Makes Someone "Devious" — The Three Key Ingredients

Cleverness. A devious person is not carelessly or stupidly dishonest. They are smart about their dishonesty. They plan ahead, think several steps forward, and carefully construct ways to deceive others. This is what separates devious from simply being a bad liar. A devious person is, in a twisted way, a skilled one.

Indirectness. A devious person never goes straight for their goal in an open way. They approach it from hidden angles. They might say one thing while meaning another, pretend to help you while secretly benefiting themselves, or set up a situation in which you end up doing exactly what they wanted — without even realizing it.

Deception. At the center of everything devious is the act of hiding one's true intentions. A devious person wants you to believe something that is not the whole truth. They wear a mask of innocence, friendship, or neutrality, while secretly working an agenda underneath.

When all three of these ingredients come together — cleverness, indirectness, and deception — you have something devious.
A Second (Less Common) Meaning

In older, more literary English, devious can also describe a path, road, or route that is not straight — one that wanders, curves, or winds in unpredictable directions. For example, "They followed a devious trail through the mountains." This meaning is rare in everyday modern conversation, but you may encounter it in classic novels or formal writing. It connects logically to the main meaning: just as a devious path bends away from a straight line, a devious person bends away from a straight, honest approach.
Devious in Real Sentences

Here are examples that show the word in action:

  • "She had a devious plan to make her colleague look bad in front of the boss, while appearing completely innocent herself."
  • "Don't trust him — he has a devious mind and always has a hidden agenda."
  • "The devious politician smiled warmly at voters while secretly working against their interests."
  • "The child had a devious grin as he hid his sister's toy and pretended not to know where it was."
  • "It was a devious scheme — so cleverly constructed that nobody suspected anything until it was too late."

Notice in each example that there is always a layer of hiddenness combined with intent. The deception is not accidental — it is planned.
What "Devious" Is NOT

Understanding what a word does not mean is just as important.

Devious is not the same as simply being wrong or making a mistake. A person who accidentally gives you wrong information is not devious. Devious requires intent — the person must be deliberately choosing to deceive or manipulate.

Devious is not the same as openly aggressive or rude. Someone who loudly argues, threatens you, or insults you to your face is being confrontational — but not devious. Devious behavior is hidden, not open. A devious person smiles while they stab you in the back.

Devious is not the same as simply being private or secretive. A shy person who keeps to themselves is not devious. The key is that a devious person's secrecy is weaponized — they use it to manipulate or deceive others for their own gain.
Words That Are Similar — and How They Differ

Cunning — Similar to devious, but cunning focuses more on sheer cleverness and craft. A cunning person is sharp and shrewd. Devious adds a stronger sense of moral wrongness and hidden dishonesty.

Sly — A sly person is clever in a quiet, hidden way — aware of things others miss, and careful not to be caught. Sly is slightly lighter in tone than devious. A sly smile or a sly joke can sometimes even be used playfully. Devious is almost always negative.

Scheming — A scheming person is always plotting and planning secret strategies. Scheming is very close to devious but emphasizes the action of planning. Devious describes both the character and the behavior.

Manipulative — A manipulative person controls others through emotional tricks, pressure, or false information. Devious is the broader word (it includes the cleverness and indirectness), while manipulative focuses specifically on the act of controlling others.

Deceitful — A deceitful person simply lies or creates false impressions. Devious is deceitful plus clever planning and indirect methods. All devious people are deceitful, but not all deceitful people are devious.
The Opposite of Devious

Someone who is the opposite of devious is straightforward, honest, transparent, or candid — they say exactly what they mean, do exactly what they say, and have nothing to hide. You always know where you stand with them.
The Tone and Connotation

Calling someone or something devious is always negative. It is never a compliment. Even when used humorously — like saying a child's prank was "devious" with a smile — the word still carries the clear sense of sneaky and dishonest behavior. It carries a stronger moral judgment than just calling someone "tricky" or "clever." It suggests a deliberate choice to be dishonest, which is why it reflects poorly on a person's character.
Common Collocations (Words Devious Is Often Paired With)

In real usage, you will often see devious paired with words like these: a devious plan, a devious scheme, a devious mind, a devious smile, a devious plot, a devious trick, or a devious person. These pairings reinforce the sense of something carefully thought-out and intentionally hidden.
The Single-Sentence Summary

If you had to boil it all down to one sentence:

Devious means using clever, hidden, and dishonest methods to achieve a goal, while hiding your true intentions from others.
DEE-vee-uhs
